title: Telemetry has two stores: SQLite for transcripts, Loki for events

statements.says: Studio reads skill usage from two stores: transcripts in SQLite and events in Loki.
A background job parses the transcripts once into SQLite and keeps up with new sessions.
Claude Code sends OTLP to an OpenTelemetry Collector, which forwards to Loki.
Skillworks.Core queries Loki's /loki/api/v1/query_range over HttpClient.
The Collector and Loki containers are Aspire resources with a persistent lifetime and a data volume, so they keep catching events after the AppHost stops.
The containers' host ports are pinned and unproxied.
The two stores join on skill name and time, in C#, not in a database.
The hand-started claude-loki, claude-grafana and claude-renderer containers predate this decision and must be removed.
Studio writes the OTEL_* block into ~/.claude/settings.json itself, merging rather than replacing and asking before the first write.
The collector's host port is pinned so the value written to the settings stays stable across runs.
Every assistant record in the transcripts carries attributionSkill beside the full usage block, so cost per skill is already on disk and needs nothing switched on.
The transcripts on this machine hold 678 MB across 1471 files, far too much to reparse per request.
Transcripts are the durable record: they exist whether or not Studio is running.
Transcripts do not say where a skill came from, while the skill_activated log event carries skill.source, plugin.name and marketplace.name.
That provenance is what tells an engine from an entry point once the catalogue ships as a plugin.
The ports are unproxied because Aspire's proxy holds the port and then dies with the AppHost.
The Collector is there for the seam: dropping noisy events, renaming fields and fanning out to a second sink later are all collector config, invisible to Claude Code and to Studio.
The old containers must go because Aspire's Loki wants port 3100, which the old one holds.
Nothing is emitted until ~/.claude/settings.json carries the OTEL_* variables, which is why Studio writes them.
A single store was the tempting alternative and was not chosen; the two stores join on skill name and time in C#, not in a database, which is the cost of the split.
Grafana is not part of this, because Studio is the dashboard and a second UI over the same data is waste.
